Today Apple celebrates the opening of its advanced manufacturing center in Houston, Texas. Here are the details.

Apple will train business leaders at new Houston advanced manufacturing center

Apple today opened its brand new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center offers free training and educational courses to small and medium-sized businesses, giving them hands-on experience with cutting-edge equipment, interactive labs and various tools to accelerate innovation. The AMC is located within the same Houston facility that produces and ships Apple's advanced AI servers and will begin producing Mac mini later this year. […] Apple CEO Tim Cook said: "In just nine months, we've invested hundreds of millions of dollars here in this Houston facility. We've built the factory, started production lines, and already shipped the first batch of advanced AI servers. Today, we're thrilled to open this new Advanced Manufacturing Center, a place where business leaders, workers and students can learn about the innovative processes we use to build Apple's most breakthrough products. We're also looking forward to starting Mac mini production later this year. We believe in American workers and American ingenuity, and we're moving at remarkable speed, because we don't just want to create great products — we want to build the future of American manufacturing."

Tim Cook said on social media that he made a special trip to Houston for the opening ceremony. The launch event will be attended by several government officials, including US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, US Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, US Congressman Christian Menefee, Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis, among others.

The AMC spans 20,000 square feet, where Apple's experts will "share their knowledge directly with participating businesses and entrepreneurs to help advance smart manufacturing across America."

The first group of business leaders arrived today to take part in the very first training session. Today's focus is on smart manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
